title: Market Capitalization
description: How do we measure the true size of a company?

slides.title: Price vs Size
slides.content: A stock priced at $100 isn't necessarily a 'bigger' company than a stock priced at $50. It depends on how many total shares exist.

slides.title: The Formula
slides.content: Market Cap = (Current Stock Price) × (Total Number of Outstanding Shares). This is the total price tag to buy the entire company.

slides.title: Categories
slides.content: Mega-cap (Apple, Microsoft), Large-cap (over $10B), Mid-cap ($2B to $10B), and Small-cap (under $2B).

quiz.question: Company A has 1 million shares at $100. Company B has 10 million shares at $20. Which company is 'bigger' (higher market cap)?

options.explanation: B is worth 200 million (10m x $20). A is only worth 100 million (1m x $100).
